entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10925"/><div sID="gen19675" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10925"/>5. Literally, "On our necks we are persecuted"; that is, Men tread on our necks (<reference osisRef="Ps.66.12">Psa 66:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.51.23">Is 51:23</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Josh.10.24">Jos 10:24</reference>). The extremest oppression. The foe not merely galled the Jews face, back, and sides, but their neck. A just retribution, as they had been stiff in neck against the yoke of God (<reference osisRef="2Chr.30.8">2Ch 30:8</reference>, Margin; <reference osisRef="Neh.9.29">Ne 9:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.48.4">Is 48:4</reference>). <div eID="gen19675" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 5. Literally, "On our necks we are persecuted"; that is, Men tread on our necks ( Psa 66:12 ; Is 51:23 ; compare Jos 10:24 ). The extremest oppression. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10928"/><div sID="gen19682" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10928"/><hi type="bold">8. Servants ... ruled ... us--</hi>Servants under the Chaldean governors ruled the Jews (<reference osisRef="Neh.5.15">Ne 5:15</reference>). Israel, once a "kingdom of priests" (<reference osisRef="Exod.19.6">Ex 19:6</reference>), is become like Canaan, "a servant of servants," according to the curse (<reference osisRef="Gen.9.25">Ge 9:25</reference>). The Chaldeans were designed to be "servants" of Shem, being descended from Ham (<reference osisRef="Gen.9.26">Ge 9:26</reference>). Now through the Jews' sin, their positions are reversed. <div eID="gen19682" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10940"/><div sID="gen19697" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10940"/>21. (<reference osisRef="Ps.80.3">Psa 80:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.18">Jr 31:18</reference>). "Restore us to favor with Thee, and so we shall be restored to our old position" [Grotius]. Jeremiah is not speaking of spiritual conversion, but of that outward turning whereby God receives men into His fatherly favor, manifested in bestowing prosperity [Calvin]. Still, as Israel is a type of the Church, temporal goods typify spiritual blessings; and so the sinner may use this prayer for God to convert him. <div eID="gen19697" type="x-p"/>
